about: SEC-STD: what each standard asks of the settings eFa-next touches. Services: web (nginx 443), submission (587/465), mail_in (port 25, opportunistic), mail_out (outgoing). Each standard names its document, version and whether the values were checked against that version.

deliberate.why: owner decision 2026-11-12: eFa-next keeps the quantum-safe hybrid key exchange; "on": false makes the check and the SSH profile strictly BSI (the table below is then not used).

equivalents.about: Values outside a standard's list that count as fulfilling it, each with the source; only these, never by guess. relation: stronger or equal; than: the listed value it is measured against.

X25519MLKEM768.why: hybrid of X25519 and ML-KEM-768: secure as long as one of both holds, and against quantum computers
refs: RFC 10024 (PQ/T hybrid key agreement for TLS 1.3, 2026)

X25519.why: about 128 bits of security, the same level as P-256

mlkem768x25519-sha256.why: hybrid of X25519 and ML-KEM-768 for SSH: secure as long as one of both holds, and against quantum computers
refs: RFC 10042 (PQ/T hybrid key exchange with ML-KEM in SSH, 2026)

brainpoolP256r1.why: a 256-bit curve of the same level as P-256, asked for by BSI TR-03116-4

brainpoolP256r1tls13.why: brainpoolP256r1 for TLS 1.3, the same level as P-256, asked for by BSI TR-03116-4
